extra.message: User-controlled GET parameter 'host' is concatenated directly into an os.system() call ('ping -c 1 ' + host). An attacker can inject arbitrary shell commands (e.g., host='127.0.0.1; cat /etc/passwd'), achieving remote command execution on the server.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: User-controlled GET parameter 'expr' is passed directly to eval(). Even with __builtins__ restricted to {}, Python object graph traversal (e.g., via ().__class__.__base__.__subclasses__()) allows sandbox escape and arbitrary code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: User-controlled GET parameter 'fragment' is concatenated into a Jinja2 Template and rendered. This is server-side template injection: payloads like {{ config }} or {{ ''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__() }} allow data exfiltration and remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: pickle.loads() is called on raw bytes taken directly from the request body or the 'blob' GET parameter (optionally base64-decoded). Deserializing attacker-controlled pickle data results in arbitrary remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data

extra.message: A JSON 'filter' taken from the request body is passed unmodified to pymongo's find_one(). An attacker can supply MongoDB operator payloads such as {"$gt": ""} or {"$where": "..."} to bypass query logic and extract arbitrary records (NoSQL injection).

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: lxml etree.XMLParser is configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False and then used to parse the raw request body. This allows XML External Entity (XXE) attacks: reading local files, SSRF to internal/network hosts, and denial of service via entity expansion.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: case_client_fold_108 is the only ops endpoint that omits the _wrk_gate() internal-token check applied to all sibling endpoints. It is registered as a public route in legalcase/urls.py and discloses internal case operations data (case counts and an ops memo referencing owner contact details) to any unauthenticated requester.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: api_matter_detail fetches any Matter by primary key with only a role check (non-client). Unlike api_matters, it never restricts the object to matters the attorney/paralegal is assigned to, so any authenticated staff user can read any matter's description, sensitivity, client, and attorney by iterating IDs (IDOR / broken object-level authorization).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The 'lane' GET/POST parameter is passed unvalidated to django.shortcuts.redirect(). An attacker can supply an absolute external URL (e.g., lane=https://evil.example) causing an open redirect usable for phishing and credential theft.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: The view logs the full request body together with the caller's 'authorization' header (bearer token) at WARNING level. Writing session/authorization credentials to application logs exposes them to anyone with log access (CWE-532).

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The 'count' GET parameter is converted with int() and used to build a list of that many dicts with no upper bound. A request with a huge count (e.g., count=100000000) forces excessive CPU/memory consumption, enabling denial of service (uncontrolled resource consumption).

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: The view deliberately raises an exception embedding the user-supplied 'ref' and the server's absolute filesystem path (BASE_EXPORT_DIR), then returns the exception text and class name in a 500 JSON response. This leaks internal path and error details to the requester.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Authentication verifiers are hardcoded in source: known = {"north": "4812", "south": "5930"}. These short numeric secrets are embedded in the repository and compared directly against the user-supplied 'verifier' parameter, constituting hardcoded credentials.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: The request's Origin header (defaulting to '*') is reflected verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin while Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is set to 'true'. Any website can then make credentialed cross-origin requests to this endpoint and read the response, enabling cross-origin data theft.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The response explicitly disables browser XSS protection (X-XSS-Protection: 0) and empties the Content-Security-Policy header, deliberately weakening client-side protection mechanisms for content served by this endpoint.

cwe: CWE-693: Protection Mechanism Failure

extra.message: Security codes/nonces are generated with random.choice() from the non-cryptographic 'random' module (Mersenne Twister), whose output is predictable. cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

extra.message: An unverified SSL context (ssl._create_unverified_context()) is used for an outbound HTTPS request to a partner endpoint, disabling certificate and hostname verification. This permits man-in-the-middle interception and tampering of the partner communication.

cwe: CWE-295: Improper Certificate Validation

extra.message: The endpoint returns a hardcoded trace flag together with the DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE value and the server's absolute BASE_EXPORT_DIR filesystem path, disclosing internal configuration and path information useful for further attacks.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: Files (or raw request bodies with an attacker-controlled 'packet_ref' name) are saved to disk with no validation of file type, extension, or content. This unrestricted upload can be used to store dangerous files (e.g., executable or script content) on the server.

extra.message: client_message_approve changes a ClientMessage to 'approved' and marks it client-visible on a plain GET request; templates/matters/attorney_dashboard.html:119 links to it with a simple anchor and no CSRF token. cwe: CWE-352: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)

extra.message: deadline_complete marks a deadline completed on a plain GET request; templates/deadlines/deadline_detail.html:18 and deadline_list.html:57 invoke it via anchor links without CSRF tokens, allowing cross-site request forgery that alters deadline status.

extra.message: client_message_send has no role or permission check beyond @login_required: any authenticated user (including users with the 'client' role) can fetch any ClientMessage by pk and transition an approved message to 'sent', triggering delivery to a client. extra.message: privileged_note_create only checks the role-based can_write_privileged_notes(); it then attaches a privileged note to whatever Matter pk is supplied via GET/POST without verifying the attorney has access to that matter (unlike can_access_matter used elsewhere). extra.message: User-controlled matter fields (title, client name, etc.) are written directly into CSV cells without sanitizing leading '=', '+', '-', or '@' characters. When the exported CSV is opened in a spreadsheet application, crafted values can execute formulas (CSV/formula injection).

extra.message: SECRET_KEY falls back to the hardcoded value 'django-insecure-change-me' when the environment variable is unset. A predictable SECRET_KEY allows forging of signed session cookies, password-reset tokens, and other signed data if deployed without the env override.
